# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization – Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**RE: Denial dated 2026-08-04 | Reference Number POC-6E16FAD700-45453 | Member ID W670697505**

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which was denied on 2026-08-04 for "incomplete documentation." I am asking that this decision be reconsidered. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in my file meet the plan's own published criteria under **Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy** (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html, last review 12/11/2025).

## How my records meet the plan's criteria

The plan's policy states:

> "Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:"

The procedure my surgeon requested, CPT 28296, is a bony correction bunionectomy for symptomatic hallux valgus. [Please confirm my age/date of birth is on file to establish that I am 18 years of age or older and skeletally mature, as required by this section.]

The policy also states:

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

and

> "Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:"

My records show progressive foot pain for 24 months that has not been relieved by rest. During that time I completed a structured course of conservative treatment under professional supervision, including:

- NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-25, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief
- Activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, with 18 physical therapy visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21), documented in the physical therapy discharge note
- Weight-bearing foot X-rays on 2026-06-29 showing a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees
- Documented functional limitations, including an inability to tolerate closed shoes and a risk of ulceration over the bony prominence
- A physical exam with positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side

Taken together, these records document persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment supervised by a healthcare professional, consistent with the policy language above.

I want to note that some of the criteria listed in connection with my denial — including "Minimum follow-up was at least 12 months," and the language about arthrodesis, failed Keller bunionectomy, and fusion for advanced degenerative disease — appear from the policy excerpts to relate to a different, more advanced clinical scenario (arthrodesis or revision after failed prior surgery) and to post-surgical outcome tracking, rather than to the initial bony correction bunionectomy my surgeon requested. If these sections were applied to my case, I would ask that Aetna clarify how they apply, since my request is for a first-time bunionectomy, not a fusion or revision procedure, and I have had no prior bunion surgery on this foot.

## What I am asking for

I am requesting that Aetna reconsider the denial of CPT 28296 in light of the clinical documentation summarized above, and approve the prior authorization for my bunion surgery. If any additional records — such as the full physical therapy notes, imaging report, or surgeon's clinical note — would help complete the file, please let me know specifically what is needed so my provider's office can send it promptly.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-01-31** (180 days from the date of this notice). I plan to submit this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available through my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379. I will confirm the correct appeal address printed on my denial letter before sending it, and I may also call 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member ID card with questions.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
Date: [insert date]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Address: [insert address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
